key_insight: Optical-fiber daylighting can substantially cut vertical-farm electricity use, but present fiber costs and crop-yield tradeoffs keep it from being economically competitive with LEDs or rooftop PV.
engineering_relevance: The paper provides a systems-level benchmark for integrating concentrated sunlight into vertical farms, helping engineers compare optical-fiber daylighting, light pipes, and PV under real crop-growth and cost constraints.
method: Coupled a validated transient vertical-farm model with Tonatiuh ray-tracing of a single-axis tracked Fresnel concentrator.
Compared five optical-fiber types and three daylighting strategies against light-pipe and rooftop-PV baselines.
Evaluated useful-PAR delivery, crop production, specific electrical energy consumption, and light cost.
evidence_signal: The optical-fiber system delivered 19–27% annual useful-PAR efficiency and reduced electricity consumption by 35–89%, but daylight-only operation lowered crop productivity by 52% and current costs require roughly a 90% capital-cost reduction to compete.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on fiber type and strategy, and the approach may be limited by high upfront fiber cost plus productivity penalties when daylight fully replaces LEDs.
paper_title: Can sunlight replace LEDs in vertical farms? A critical assessment of optical-fiber daylighting strategies
